o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish طوتمق (dutmaq), from Proto-Turkic *tut-. Cognate with Old Turkic 𐱃𐰆𐱃 (tut-, “to keep, catch, own”), Turkish tutmak (“to catch, keep”), Bashkir тотоу (tutuw, “to keep, hold”), Chuvash тытма (tytma, “to keep, hold”), Khakas & Shor тударға (tudarğa, “to keep, hold, catch, seize, rule, hold back”), Kyrgyz тутуу (tutuu, “to catch”), Turkmen tutmak (“to hold, keep, catch, hire, fill”), Tuvan тудар (tudar, “to hold, catch, grab”), Uzbek tutmoq (“to take, hold, catch”), Yakut тут (tut, “to hold, seize, grab, catch”).

From Proto-Common Turkic *uša- (“small”), alternatively reconstructed as *uvša-.
Cognate with Turkish uşah (“child”) (dialectal, Zonguldak, Bartın, Karabük, the Black Sea Region, Kırşehir), uşak (“male child”) (dialectal, Ordu), and Gagauz uşak (“child”).
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آزاد ایتمك (āzād etmäk).
